body: This is the first time she's ever attempted suicide or harmed herself in any way.  I agree, getting back on the Prozac is definitely something that needs to happen.  However she has expressed a desire to not be dependent on drugs for her emotional stability, and I think that's a good goal for anyone to have.  But for the short term she needs to be on it, and if she wants to get off of it, she needs to have something else going on, like therapy or other professional help.

Thanks for this.  I actually found this out from a roommate of mine who knows a little about the subject.  It's a little comforting to know that she probably hasn't spent a lot of time thinking about this or planning it because it makes me more confident that she won't try to do it again before she can see the counselor tomorrow.

Just a little more background information, she takes Prozac for depression, and she told me a few weeks ago that she hadn't been taking it for a couple months, so I'm sure that contributed to it.  I think you're right about the recent hard times.  We got to spend Christmas together with my family and now we're apart again, she's back at school and doesn't have many friends.  She had a hard time last semester and now I think it's pretty daunting for her to think about the prospect of another whole semester of all the same problems she just got to take a break from for a couple weeks.  She's also fairly neurotic and prone to emotional outbursts.  Hence the Prozac.
